title.zh: 卷四百三十 列傳第一百八十九 道學四 朱氏門人 黃榦 李燔 張洽 陳淳 李方子 黃灝
title.en: Volume 430 Biographies 189: Taoist Scholars 4: Zhu Shimenren, Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, Huang Hao
title.raw: 卷四百三十 列傳第一百八十九 道學四 朱氏門人 黃榦 李燔 張洽 陳淳 李方子 黃灝 Volume 430 Biographies 189: Taoist Scholars 4: Zhu Shimenren, Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, Huang Hao

sentences.zh: 黃榦 李燔 張洽 陳淳 李方子 黃灝

translations.literal: Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, Huang Hao
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, and Huang Hao

sentences.zh: 黃榦字直卿，福州閩縣人。

translations.literal: Huang Gan, courtesy name Zhizhi, was a native of Min County in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gan, whose courtesy name was Zhizhi, came from Min County in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父瑀，在高宗時為監察御史，以篤行直道著聞。

translations.literal: His father Yu, who served as investigating censor under Emperor Gaozong, was renowned for his earnest conduct and upright character.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as investigating censor under Emperor Gaozong and was famed for his earnest conduct and upright ways.

sentences.zh: 瑀沒，榦往見清江劉清之。

translations.literal: After Yu died, Gan went to see Liu Qingzhi of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu died, Gan went to see Liu Qingzhi of Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 清之奇之，曰：「子乃遠器，時學非所以處子也。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi marveled at him and said, "You are a vessel for distant horizons; the learning of the age is not how one should place you."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was struck by him and said, "You are meant for great things; the conventional learning of the day is no fit place for you."

sentences.zh: 因命受業朱熹。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered him to study under Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He then told him to take Zhu Xi as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 幹家法嚴重，乃以白母，即日行。

translations.literal: Gan's household rules were strict; he informed his mother and set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's household discipline was severe; he told his mother and left that very day.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，既至而熹它出，榦因留客邸，臥起一榻，不解衣者二月，而熹始歸。

translations.literal: It was deep winter; when he arrived Xi was away on other business, so Gan lodged at a guest inn, sleeping and rising on a single couch without removing his clothes for two months, until Xi at last returned.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay deep; he reached Xi's place only to find him away, so Gan stayed at a guest inn, sleeping and waking on one couch without undressing for two months, until Xi finally came home.

sentences.zh: 榦自見熹，夜不設榻，不解帶，少倦則微坐，一倚或至達曙。

translations.literal: From the time Gan met Xi, at night he set out no couch and did not loosen his belt; when slightly weary he would sit upright, and a single lean against something might last until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was in Xi's presence he never laid out a bed at night or loosened his belt; when fatigue crept in he sat bolt upright, and one brief lean might carry him clear to daybreak.

sentences.zh: 熹語人曰：「直卿志堅思苦，與之處甚有益。」

translations.literal: Xi told others, "Zhizhi's will is firm and his thinking arduous; to be with him is of great benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Xi told others, "Zhizhi's resolve is iron and his thought relentless; company with him does one real good."

sentences.zh: 嘗詣東萊呂祖謙，以所聞於熹者相質正。

translations.literal: He once went to Donglai to see Lü Zuqian and tested what he had heard from Xi against him.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited Lü Zuqian at Donglai and cross-checked what he had learned from Xi.

sentences.zh: 及廣漢張栻亡。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shi of Guanghan died,
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shi of Guanghan passed away,

sentences.zh: 熹與榦書曰：「吾道益孤矣，所望於賢者不輕。」

translations.literal: Xi wrote to Gan, "My Way grows ever more solitary; what I expect of the worthy is no light matter."
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote to Gan, "My Way grows lonelier by the day; what I look for in a worthy man is no small thing."

sentences.zh: 後遂以其子妻榦。

translations.literal: Later he gave his daughter to Gan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gave his daughter to Gan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，熹命榦奉表，補將仕郎，銓中，授迪功郎，監台州酒務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong took the throne, Xi ordered Gan to present the memorial of felicitation; he was granted probationary gentleman, passed the selection, and was appointed probationary merit officer and supervisor of the Taizhou wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Xi had Gan present the congratulatory memorial; he was made probationary gentleman, passed civil-service selection, and received appointment as probationary merit officer supervising the Taizhou wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，學者從之講學於墓廬甚眾。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death, a great host of scholars followed him to lecture at his mourning hut by the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, a great host of scholars followed him to study at his mourning hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 熹作竹林精舍成，遺榦書，有「它時便可請直卿代即講席」之語。

translations.literal: When Xi finished the Bamboo Grove Retreat, he sent Gan a letter with the words, "When the time comes you may ask Zhizhi to take my place at the lecture seat."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi completed the Bamboo Grove Retreat he wrote Gan a letter saying, "When the time comes you may ask Zhizhi to step directly into my chair."

sentences.zh: 及編《禮書》，獨以《喪》、《祭》二編屬榦，稿成，熹見而喜曰：「所立規模次第，縝密有條理，它日當取所編家鄉、邦國、王朝禮，悉仿此更定之。」

translations.literal: When compiling the Book of Rites, he assigned only the Mourning and Sacrifice sections to Gan; when the draft was done Xi read it and said with delight, "The framework and sequence you have set are close-woven and orderly; another day we should take the village, state, and court ritual sections you have compiled and revise them all on this model."
translations.idiomatic: While editing the Book of Rites he entrusted only the Mourning and Sacrifice volumes to Gan; when the draft was finished Xi read it with delight and said, "The scale and sequence you have laid down are tight and orderly; one day we should take the village, state, and court ritual sections and rework them all on this pattern."

sentences.zh: 病革，以深衣及所著書授榦，手書與訣曰：「吾道之托在此，吾無憾矣。」

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical he handed Gan his deep robe and his writings, and wrote in his own hand at parting, "The entrustment of my Way rests here; I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: As his illness turned grave he gave Gan his deep robe and his books, and wrote in his own hand at farewell, "The trust of my Way is placed here; I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 訃聞，榦持心喪三年畢，調監嘉興府石門酒庫。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, Gan observed heart-mourning for three full years, then was transferred to supervise the Shimen wine depot in Jiaxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the death notice came, Gan kept heart-mourning for three full years, then was reassigned to supervise the Shimen wine depot in Jiaxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄方謀用兵，吳獵帥湖北，將赴鎮，訪以兵事。

translations.literal: At that time Han Tuozhou was plotting to use force; Wu Lie, commander of Hubei, was about to take up his post and consulted Gan on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Tuozhou was plotting war; Wu Lie, commanding Hubei, was about to take up his post and asked Gan about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 榦曰：「聞議者謂今天下欲為大舉深入之謀，果爾，必敗。

translations.literal: Gan said, "I hear the counsellors say the empire today intends a great thrust deep into enemy territory; if that is so, it must fail.
translations.idiomatic: Gan said, "I hear men at court say the realm now plans a great thrust deep into enemy country; if that is true, it is doomed to fail.

sentences.zh: 此何時而可進取哉？」

translations.literal: What season is this in which one may advance and seize?"
translations.idiomatic: What season is this for advancing and seizing ground?"

sentences.zh: 獵雅敬榦名德，辟為荊湖北路安撫司激賞酒庫兼準備差遣，事有未當，必輸忠款力爭。

translations.literal: Lie, who greatly respected Gan's reputation and virtue, appointed him to the Jing-Shang wine depot of the Hubei pacification commission with additional duty as preparatory dispatch; whenever policy was wrong he would offer loyal remonstrance and strive to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, who deeply respected Gan's name and virtue, appointed him to the Jing-Shang wine depot of the Hubei pacification commission with additional preparatory dispatch; whenever anything was amiss he offered loyal remonstrance and fought it through.

sentences.zh: 江西提舉常平趙希懌、知撫州高商老辟為臨川令，歲旱，勸糶捕蝗極其力。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiyi, Jiangxi intendant for ever-normal granaries, and Gao Shanglao, prefect of Fuzhou, appointed him magistrate of Linchuan; in a year of drought he urged grain sales and locust-catching to the limit of his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiyi, Jiangxi intendant for ever-normal granaries, and Gao Shanglao, prefect of Fuzhou, made him magistrate of Linchuan; in a drought year he pressed grain sales and locust-catching with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 改知新淦縣，吏民習知臨川之政，皆喜，不令而政行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Xin'gan County; officials and people, accustomed to Linchuan's governance, were all pleased, and government went forward without need of orders.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to administer Xin'gan County; officials and people, knowing Linchuan's rule, were delighted, and government ran without fresh orders.

sentences.zh: 以提舉常平郡太守薦，擢監尚書六部門，未上，改差通判安豐軍。

translations.literal: On recommendation of the intendant for ever-normal granaries and the prefect, he was promoted to supervisor of the Six Ministries Gate at the Secretariat; before he took up the post he was reassigned as vice-prefect of Anfeng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by the intendant for ever-normal granaries and the prefect, he was raised to supervisor of the Six Ministries Gate; before he reported he was reassigned vice-prefect of Anfeng Army.

sentences.zh: 淮西帥司檄榦鞫和州獄，獄故以疑未決，榦釋囚桎梏飲食之，委曲審問無所得。

translations.literal: The Huai-Xi commandery ordered Gan to try a Hezhou prison case; the case had long hung in doubt unresolved; Gan released the prisoners from shackles and fed them, questioning them minutely yet learning nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-Xi command ordered Gan to try a Hezhou prison case long left doubtful; Gan freed the prisoners from fetters and fed them, questioning them at length yet learning nothing.

sentences.zh: 一夜，夢井中有人，明日呼囚詰之曰：「汝殺人，投之於井，我悉知之矣，胡得欺我。」

translations.literal: One night he dreamed of someone in a well; the next day he called the prisoner and said, "You killed a man and cast him into a well; I know it all—how dare you deceive me?"
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed of someone in a well; next day he summoned the prisoner and said, "You killed a man and threw him down a well; I know everything—how dare you lie to me?"

sentences.zh: 囚遂驚服，果於廢井得屍。

translations.literal: The prisoner in alarm confessed; indeed a corpse was found in an abandoned well.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoner confessed in alarm; a corpse was indeed found in an abandoned well.

sentences.zh: 尋知漢陽軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Hanyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 值歲飢，糴客米、發常平以振。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he bought guest grain and opened the ever-normal granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he bought grain from merchants and opened ever-normal stores for relief.

sentences.zh: 制置司下令，欲移本軍之粟而禁其糴，榦報以乞候榦罷然後施行，及援鄂州例，十之一告糴於制司。

translations.literal: The pacification commission issued an order wishing to move this army's grain while forbidding purchases; Gan replied asking to wait until after he left office before enforcing it, and citing the Ezhou precedent, reported one-tenth of purchases to the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification office ordered grain moved out of the command while banning local purchase; Gan asked that enforcement wait until he left office, and citing the Ezhou precedent reported one-tenth of purchases to the commission.

sentences.zh: 荒政具舉。

translations.literal: Famine administration was fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Famine relief was fully carried out.

sentences.zh: 旁郡饑民輻湊，惠撫均一，春暖願歸者給之糧，不願者結廬居之，民大感悅。

translations.literal: Starving people from neighboring prefectures converged; he treated them with equal kindness; when spring warmed, those who wished to return were given grain, those who did not were given huts to dwell in, and the people were deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from neighboring prefectures poured in; he treated them alike; when spring came those who wished to go home received grain, those who stayed were given shelters, and the people were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 所至以重庠序，先教養。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he gave weight to schools and put nurture first.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he stressed schools and put nurture first.

sentences.zh: 其在漢陽，即郡治後鳳棲山為屋，館四方士，立周、程、游、朱四先生祠。

translations.literal: At Hanyang he built houses on Phoenix Perch Hill behind the prefectural seat to lodge scholars from all quarters, and established shrines to the four masters Zhou, Cheng, You, and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanyang he built halls on Phoenix Perch Hill behind the yamen to lodge scholars from afar and raised shrines to Zhou, the Cheng brothers, You, and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 以病乞祠，主管武夷沖祐觀。

translations.literal: He begged leave on grounds of illness and was made custodian of Chongyou Abbey on Mount Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He sought leave on grounds of illness and was made custodian of Chongyou Abbey on Mount Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 尋起知安慶府，至則金人破光山，而沿邊多警。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to administer Anqing Prefecture; when he arrived the Jin had broken Guangshan and alarms ran along the border.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to Anqing; when he arrived the Jin had taken Guangshan and the frontier was alight with alarm.

sentences.zh: 安慶去光山不遠，民情震恐。

translations.literal: Anqing was not far from Guangshan, and the people were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing lay close to Guangshan, and popular fear ran high.

sentences.zh: 乃請於朝，城安慶以備戰守，不俟報，即日興工。

translations.literal: He petitioned the court to wall Anqing for defense; without waiting for reply he began work the same day.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to wall Anqing for defense; without awaiting reply he began work that same day.

sentences.zh: 城分十二料，先自築一料，計其工費若干，然後委官吏、寓公、士人分料主之。

translations.literal: The wall was divided into twelve sections; he first built one section himself, calculating its cost, then assigned officials, resident notables, and gentlemen to take charge of sections.
translations.idiomatic: The wall was split into twelve sections; he built one section first, reckoned its cost, then assigned officials, local notables, and gentry to each section.

sentences.zh: 役民兵五千人，人役九十日，而計人戶產錢起丁夫，通役二萬夫，人十日而罷。

translations.literal: He drafted five thousand militiamen, each serving ninety days; by household wealth he also raised twenty thousand corvée laborers, each serving ten days and then released.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted five thousand militiamen for ninety days each; by household wealth he raised twenty thousand corvée men for ten days each.

sentences.zh: 役者更番，暑月月休六日，日午休一時，至秋漸殺其半。

translations.literal: The workers rotated in shifts; in summer they rested six days a month and one hour at noon each day; by autumn the rest was halved.
translations.idiomatic: Crews rotated; in summer they rested six days a month and one hour at noon; by autumn rest was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 榦日以五鼓坐於堂，濠砦官入聽命，以一日成算授之：役某鄉民兵若干，某鄉人夫若干；

translations.literal: Each day at the fifth drum Gan sat in the hall; moat-and-bastion officers received orders, and he gave them the day's plan: draft so many militia from such a township, so many laborers from such a township;
translations.idiomatic: Each dawn at the fifth drum Gan sat in hall; moat officers took orders and received the day's plan: draft so many militia from one township, so many laborers from another;

sentences.zh: 分佈於某人料分，或搬運某處土木，應副某料使用；

translations.literal: assign them to such-and-such a section head, or move timber and earth to such a place for use in such a section;
translations.idiomatic: post them under a given section head, or haul timber and earth to a given section;

sentences.zh: 某料民兵人夫合當更代，合散幾日錢米。

translations.literal: when militia and laborers of a section should rotate, and how much cash and grain to disburse on dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: when a section's militia and laborers should rotate, and how much cash and grain to pay on release.

sentences.zh: 俱受命畢，乃治府事，理民訟，接賓客，閱士卒，會僚佐講究邊防利病，次則巡城視役，晚入書院講論經史。

translations.literal: When orders were complete he handled prefectural business, judged lawsuits, received guests, reviewed troops, met staff to discuss border strengths and weaknesses, then inspected the wall and works, and in the evening lectured on the classics in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Orders given, he turned to prefectural affairs, lawsuits, guests, troop review, staff conferences on border ills, wall inspection, and evening lectures in the academy.

sentences.zh: 築城之杵，用錢監未鑄之鐵，事畢還之。

translations.literal: Tamping poles for the wall used unminted iron from the mint; when the work ended it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wall tampers used unminted iron from the mint; when work ended the metal went back.

sentences.zh: 城成，會上元日張燈，士民扶老攜幼，往來不絕。

translations.literal: When the wall was finished, on the Lantern Festival lights were hung and old and young came and went without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When the wall stood, Lantern Festival lights drew old and young in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 有老嫗百歲，二子輿之，諸孫從，至府致謝。

translations.literal: A woman of a hundred years was carried in a litter by two sons, her grandsons following, and came to the yamen to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: A centenarian was borne in a litter by two sons, grandsons following, to thank him at the yamen.

sentences.zh: 榦禮之，命具酒炙，且勞以金帛。

translations.literal: Gan received her with ceremony, ordered wine and meat prepared, and rewarded her with silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gan received her with ceremony, ordered wine and meat, and offered silk.

sentences.zh: 嫗曰：「老婦之來，為一郡生靈謝耳，太守之賜非所冀也。」

translations.literal: The old woman said, "I come not suited for the prefect's gift but to thank you on behalf of a whole commandery's lives."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I come to thank you for a whole commandery's lives, not suited for the prefect's bounty."

sentences.zh: 不受而去。

translations.literal: She would not accept and left.
translations.idiomatic: She refused the gifts and left.

sentences.zh: 是歲大旱，榦祈輒雨，或未出，晨興登郡閣，望灊山再拜，雨即至。

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; when Gan prayed rain came at once; if it had not yet fallen he would rise at dawn, climb the prefectural tower, bow toward Mount Qian, and rain followed.
translations.idiomatic: That year drought was severe; his prayers brought rain; if rain delayed he rose at dawn, climbed the tower, bowed toward Mount Qian, and rain came.

sentences.zh: 後二年，金人破黃州沙窩諸關，淮東、西皆震，獨安慶按堵如故。

translations.literal: Two years later the Jin broke the passes at Huangzhou Shawan; Huai East and West were shaken, yet Anqing alone remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the Jin broke Huangzhou Shawan passes; both Huai regions shook, yet Anqing alone stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 繼而霖潦餘月，巨浸暴至，城屹然無虞。

translations.literal: Then floods lasted months; a great inundation surged in, yet the wall stood firm without harm.
translations.idiomatic: Months of rain followed; floodwaters rose, yet the wall held without harm.

sentences.zh: 舒人德之，相謂曰：「不殘於寇，不滔於水，生汝者黃父也。」

translations.literal: The people of Shu praised him, saying, "We were not ravaged by bandits nor drowned by water—the man who gave us life is Father Huang."
translations.idiomatic: Shu people said, "Neither bandits nor flood destroyed us—Father Huang gave us life."

sentences.zh: 制置李珏辟為參議官，再辭不受。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Li Jue appointed him consulting officer; he declined twice and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Li Jue made him consulting officer; twice he declined.

sentences.zh: 既而朝命與徐僑兩易和州，且令先赴制府稟議，榦即日解印趨制府。

translations.literal: Then the court ordered him and Xu Qiao to exchange posts at Hezhou and to report first to the pacification office for consultation; Gan surrendered his seal that day and hurried to the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court then swapped him with Xu Qiao at Hezhou and ordered him to the pacification office first; Gan surrendered his seal and went at once.

sentences.zh: 和州人日望其來，曰：「是嘗檄至吾郡鞫死囚、感夢於井中者，庶能直吾屈乎。」

translations.literal: Hezhou people daily looked for his coming, saying, "This is the man who once came under order to try a capital case and was moved by a dream of someone in a well—perhaps he can right our wrongs."
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou people awaited him, saying, "This is he who once tried a capital case here and was moved by a dream of someone in a well—perhaps he can right our wrongs."

sentences.zh: 先是，榦移書珏曰：「丞相誅韓之後，懲意外之變，專用左右親信之人，往往得罪於天下公議。

translations.literal: Earlier Gan had written to Jue, "After the chief minister executed Han, fearing unforeseen change, he relied solely on close favorites; they have often offended public opinion under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gan wrote Jue, "After the chief minister killed Han, fearing surprise, he relied only on close favorites who have often offended public opinion.

sentences.zh: 世之君子遂從而歸咎於丞相，丞相不堪其咎，繼然逐去之，而左右親信者其用愈專矣。

translations.literal: Men of worth in the world then turned to blame the chief minister; unable to bear the blame, he drove them off one after another, while the close favorites' power grew ever more exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men blamed the chief minister; unable to bear it he drove them away, while favorites grew more exclusive.

sentences.zh: 平居無事，紀綱紊亂，不過州縣之間，百姓受禍。

translations.literal: In ordinary times when nothing was amiss, discipline was chaotic no further than the level of prefecture and county, and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In quiet times discipline broke down to county level and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 至於軍政不修，邊備廢弛，皆此曹為之，若今大敵在境，更不改圖，大事去矣。

translations.literal: As for neglected military affairs and slack border defense, these men were responsible; with a great enemy at the frontier, if no change is made, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Military neglect and slack borders were their work; with the enemy at the gate, without change the cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 今日之急，莫大於此。」

translations.literal: Today's urgency is nowhere greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: Today's urgency is nowhere greater than this."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今日之計，莫若用兩淮之人，食兩淮之粟，守兩淮之地。

translations.literal: He also said, "Today's plan is none better than using men of the two Huai, eating grain of the two Huai, defending land of the two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The plan for today is to use men of the two Huai, eat their grain, and hold their land.

sentences.zh: 然其策當先明保伍，保伍既明，則為之立堡砦，蓄馬、製軍器以資其用，不過累月，軍政可成。

translations.literal: Yet the policy must first clarify the mutual-aid system; once that is clear, build forts and stockades, store horses, and make weapons for their use—in no more than a few months military affairs may be set right.
translations.idiomatic: But policy must first clarify mutual-aid units; then build forts, keep horses, and forge arms—in a few months the army can be made whole.

sentences.zh: 且淮民遭丙寅之厄，今聞金人遷汴，莫不狼顧脅息，有棄田廬、挈妻子渡江之意，其間勇悍者。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the bingyin calamity Huai people, hearing the Jin move their capital to Bian, have looked back in fear and gasped for breath, ready to abandon fields and homes and cross the river with wives and children; among them are the fierce and bold,
translations.idiomatic: Since the bingyin disaster Huai people, hearing the Jin move to Bian, tremble and gasp, ready to abandon farms and cross the river with families; among them are fierce men,

sentences.zh: 且將伺變竊發。

translations.literal: who will watch for chance to rise in secret revolt.
translations.idiomatic: who will watch their chance to rise in secret revolt.

sentences.zh: 嚮日胡海、張軍之變，為害甚於金，今若不早為之圖，則兩淮日見荒墟，卒有警急，攘臂而起矣。」

translations.literal: The disturbances of Hu Hai and Zhang Jun in former days harmed more than the Jin; if no early plan is made, the two Huai will daily become wasteland, and at the first alarm they will throw up their arms."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hai and Zhang Jun's revolts once hurt us more than the Jin; without early planning the two Huai will become desert, and at the first alarm men will rise."

sentences.zh: 珏皆不能用。

translations.literal: Jue could use none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jue could adopt none of it.

sentences.zh: 及至制府，珏往惟揚視師，與偕行，榦言：「敵既退，當思所以賞功罰罪者。

translations.literal: When he reached the pacification office Jue went to Huaiyang to inspect the army and took Gan along; Gan said, "The enemy having withdrawn, one should think how to reward merit and punish guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At the pacification office Jue went to Huaiyang to inspect troops and took Gan, who said, "The enemy has withdrawn; it is time to reward merit and punish guilt.

sentences.zh: 崔惟揚能於清平山豫立義砦，斷金人右臂，方儀真能措置捍禦，不使軍民倉皇奔軼，此二人者當薦之。

translations.literal: Cui Weiyang was able at Qingpingshan to build a righteous fort in advance and cut off the Jin army's right wing; Fang Yizhen was able to arrange defense so that soldiers and people did not flee in panic—these two should be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weiyang built a fort at Qingpingshan in advance and cut the Jin right wing; Fang Yizhen organized defense so troops and people did not panic—these two should be recommended.

sentences.zh: 泗上之敗，劉倬可斬也。

translations.literal: In the defeat at Sizhou, Liu Zhuo deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sizhou defeat Liu Zhuo deserves death.

sentences.zh: 某州官吏三人攜家奔竄，追而治之，然後具奏可也。」

translations.literal: Three officials of a certain prefecture fled with their families; pursue and punish them, then memorialize the court."
translations.idiomatic: Three officials of one prefecture fled with families; pursue and punish, then memorialize."

sentences.zh: 其時幕府書館皆輕儇浮靡之士，僚吏士民有獻謀畫，多為毀抹疏駁。

translations.literal: At that time the secretariat staff were all frivolous and dissolute; when officials, clerks, gentry, or commoners offered plans, they were mostly torn up and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Then the staff were frivolous; plans from officials, clerks, gentry, or people were mostly torn up.

sentences.zh: 將帥偏，人心不附，所向無功。

translations.literal: Generals were partial and hearts did not adhere; nothing undertaken succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Generals were partisan, hearts did not unite, and nothing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 流移滿道，而諸司長吏張宴無虛日。

translations.literal: Displaced people filled the roads while the heads of departments feasted without a day free.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees clogged the roads while department heads feasted without a day free.

sentences.zh: 榦知不足與共事，歸自惟揚，再辭和州之命，仍乞祠，閉閣謝客，宴樂不與。

translations.literal: Knowing he could not work with them, Gan returned from Huaiyang, declined Hezhou again, begged a sinecure post, shut his doors to guests, and took no part in feasts or music.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not serve with them, Gan returned from Huaiyang, declined Hezhou again, begged a sinecure, shut his doors, and joined no feasts.

sentences.zh: 乃復告珏曰：

translations.literal: He again reported to Jue, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Jue again, saying:

sentences.zh: 浮光敵退已兩月，安豐已一月，盱眙亦將兩旬，不知吾所措置者何事，所施行者何策。

translations.literal: The enemy has withdrawn from Fuguang two months, Anfeng one month, and Xuyi nearly twenty days—yet what measures have we set and what policies enacted?"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy left Fuguang two months ago, Anfeng one month, Xuyi nearly twenty days—what have we done, what policy enacted?

sentences.zh: 邊備之弛，又甚於前，日復一日，恬不知懼，恐其禍又不止今春矣。

translations.literal: Border defense is laxer than before; day after day men grow complacent without fear— I fear the calamity will not stop with this spring."
translations.idiomatic: Border defense is laxer than before; day by day complacency grows—I fear disaster will not end with this spring.

sentences.zh: 向者輕信人言，為泗上之役，喪師萬人。

translations.literal: Earlier, trusting men's words, you undertook the Sizhou campaign and lost ten thousand troops."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, trusting men's words, you undertook Sizhou and lost ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 良將勁卒、精兵利器，不戰而淪於泗水，黃團老幼，俘虜殺戮五六千人，盱眙東西數百里，莽為丘墟。

translations.literal: Good generals, strong soldiers, keen arms—all fell to the Sishui without battle; old and young of Huang and Tuan, five or six thousand captured and slain; for several hundred li east and west of Xuyi the land lies waste as mounds."
translations.idiomatic: Good generals, crack troops, sharp weapons—all went to the Sishui without fighting; Huang and Tuan lost five or six thousand; for hundreds of li around Xuyi the land is ruin.

sentences.zh: 安豐、浮光之事大率類此。

translations.literal: The affairs of Anfeng and Fuguang were largely of the same kind."
translations.idiomatic: Anfeng and Fuguang were much the same.

sentences.zh: 切意千乘言旋，必痛自咎責，出宿於外，大戒於國，曰：「此吾之罪也，有能箴吾失者，疾入諫。」

translations.literal: I thought when the ruler returned he would bitterly blame himself, lodge outside the palace, and greatly warn the realm, saying, "This is my fault; whoever can admonish my errors, enter quickly and remonstrate."
translations.idiomatic: I thought on your return you would blame yourself, lodge outside, warn the realm, and say, "This is my fault; whoever can admonish me, speak at once."

sentences.zh: 日與僚屬及四方賢士討論條畫，以為後圖。

translations.literal: Daily discuss plans with staff and worthy men from all quarters for the time to come."
translations.idiomatic: Daily you would debate plans with staff and worthies from afar.

sentences.zh: 今歸已五日矣，但聞請總領、運使至玉麟堂賞牡丹，用妓樂，又聞總領、運使請宴賞亦然，又聞宴僚屬亦然。

translations.literal: Five days have passed since your return, yet I hear only of inviting the chief fiscal and transport commissioners to the Yulin Hall to view peonies with singing girls, and the same for feasts with them and with staff."
translations.idiomatic: Five days since return, yet I hear only of inviting fiscal and transport chiefs to Yulin Hall for peonies with singing girls, and the same at other feasts.

sentences.zh: 邦人諸軍聞之，豈不痛憤。

translations.literal: When the people of the command and the armies hear this, how can they not ache with rage?"
translations.idiomatic: When command people and armies hear this, how can they not rage?

sentences.zh: 且視牡丹之紅艷，豈不思邊庭之流血；

translations.literal: To look on the peonies' crimson—does one not think of blood on the border?"
translations.idiomatic: To gaze on crimson peonies—is one blind to border blood?

sentences.zh: 視管弦之啁啾，豈不思老幼之哀號；

translations.literal: To listen to pipes' twitter—does one not think of the wailing of old and young?"
translations.idiomatic: To hear pipes twitter—is one deaf to old and young wailing?

sentences.zh: 視棟宇之宏麗，豈不思士卒之暴露；

translations.literal: To view halls' grandeur—does one not think of soldiers' exposure?"
translations.idiomatic: To view grand halls—is one blind to soldiers' exposure?

sentences.zh: 視飲饌之豐美，豈不思流民之凍餒。

translations.literal: To taste rich food and drink—does one not think of refugees' hunger and cold?"
translations.idiomatic: To taste rich fare—is one deaf to refugees starving?

sentences.zh: 敵國深侵，宇內騷動，主上食不甘味，聽朝不怡；

translations.literal: The enemy invades deeply; the realm is in turmoil; the sovereign eats without savor and holds court unhappily;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy presses deep; the realm trembles; the Son of Heaven eats without taste and holds court in grief;

sentences.zh: 大臣憂懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: great ministers are anxious and know not what to do."
translations.idiomatic: ministers are anxious and know not what to do.

sentences.zh: 尚書豈得不朝夕憂懼，而乃如是之迂緩暇逸耶！

translations.literal: How can the Secretariat not worry day and night, yet be so slow, distant, and at leisure!"
translations.idiomatic: How can the Secretariat not worry day and night, yet be so slow and leisurely!

sentences.zh: 今浮光之報又至矣，金欲以十六縣之眾，四月攻浮光，侵五關，且以一縣五千人為率，則當有八萬人攻浮光，以萬人刈吾麥，以五萬人攻吾關。

translations.literal: Now word from Fuguang comes again: the Jin mean to attack with the force of sixteen counties in the fourth month, strike Fuguang, and press the five passes—at five thousand men per county that is eighty thousand against Fuguang, ten thousand to reap our wheat, fifty thousand to storm our passes."
translations.idiomatic: Word from Fuguang: the Jin will attack in the fourth month with sixteen counties—eighty thousand on Fuguang, ten thousand reaping our wheat, fifty thousand on the passes.

sentences.zh: 吾之守關不過五六百人，豈能當萬人之眾哉？

translations.literal: Our pass garrisons number no more than five or six hundred—how can they withstand ten thousand?"
translations.idiomatic: Our garrisons hold five or six hundred each—how withstand ten thousand?

sentences.zh: 則關之不可守決矣。

translations.literal: Then the passes cannot be held—that is settled."
translations.idiomatic: The passes cannot be held—that is settled.

sentences.zh: 五關失守，則蘄、黃決不可保；

translations.literal: If the five passes are lost, Qi and Huang cannot possibly be held;
translations.idiomatic: If the five passes fall, Qi and Huang cannot be held;

sentences.zh: 蘄、黃不保，則江南危。

translations.literal: if Qi and Huang are not held, then Jiangnan is in peril."
translations.idiomatic: if Qi and Huang fall, Jiangnan is in peril.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞此亦已數日，乃不聞有所施行，何耶？

translations.literal: The Secretariat has heard this for several days already, yet one hears of nothing enacted—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat has heard this for days, yet nothing is done—why?

sentences.zh: 其它言皆激切，同幕忌之尤甚，共詆排之。

translations.literal: His other words were all equally sharp; colleagues in the secretariat hated him all the more and together slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: His other words were equally sharp; secretariat colleagues hated him and slandered him together.

sentences.zh: 厥後光、黃、蘄繼失，果如其言。

translations.literal: Afterward Guang, Huang, and Qi were lost in succession, exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guang, Huang, and Qi fell in turn, just as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 遂力辭去，請祠不已。

translations.literal: He then strove to resign and begged a sinecure post without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed to leave and begged a sinecure without cease.

sentences.zh: 俄再命知安慶，不就，入廬山訪其友李燔、陳宓，相與盤旋玉淵、三峽間，俯仰其師舊跡，講《乾》、《坤》二卦於白鹿書院，山南北之士皆來集。

translations.literal: Soon he was again ordered to administer Anqing but would not go; he entered Mount Lu to visit his friends Li Fan and Chen Mi, and together they wandered between Jade Abyss and the Three Gorges, looking up and down at their teacher's old traces; he lectured on the Qian and Kun hexagrams at White Deer Academy, and scholars north and south of the mountain all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered again to Anqing but declined; he went to Mount Lu to visit Li Fan and Chen Mi, wandered Jade Abyss and the Three Gorges, traced their teacher's footsteps, lectured on Qian and Kun at White Deer Academy, and scholars from north and south of the mountain gathered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召赴行在所奏事，除大理丞，不拜，為御史李楠所劾。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the traveling court to report; he was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review but did not accept the appointment and was impeached by the censor Li Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to court; made vice director of judicial review he refused, and censor Li Nan impeached him.

sentences.zh: 初，榦入荊湖幕府，奔走諸關，與江、淮豪傑游，而豪傑往往願依榦。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gan entered the Jing-Hu secretariat, he hurried among the passes and associated with bold spirits of the Jiang and Huai regions, and such men often wished to follow Gan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan first entered the Jing-Hu secretariat he traveled the passes and mingled with Jiang-Huai heroes who often wished to follow him.

sentences.zh: 及倅安豐、武定，諸將皆歸心焉。

translations.literal: When he served as vice-prefect at Anfeng and Wuding, all the generals gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect at Anfeng and Wuding, the generals all gave him their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後倅建康，守漢陽，聲聞益著。

translations.literal: Later as vice-prefect at Jiankang and prefect of Hanyang, his fame grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Jiankang and as prefect of Hanyang his renown grew.

sentences.zh: 諸豪又深知榦倜儻有謀，及來安慶，且兼制幕，長淮軍民之心，翕然相向。

translations.literal: The bold spirits also knew well that Gan was daring and resourceful; when he came to Anqing and also held a pacification staff post, the hearts of army and people along the Long Huai turned to him as one.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes knew Gan was bold and shrewd; at Anqing, also on the pacification staff, Long Huai soldiers and people turned to him as one.

sentences.zh: 此聲既出，在位者益忌，且慮榦入見必直言邊事，以悟上意，至是群起擠之。

translations.literal: Once this reputation spread, men in power hated him all the more, fearing that if Gan were received in audience he would speak frankly on border affairs and awaken the emperor's mind; at this point they rose together to squeeze him out.
translations.idiomatic: Once this spread, those in power feared he would speak frankly on the border at audience and awaken the throne; they banded together to force him out.

sentences.zh: 榦遂歸里，弟子日盛，巴蜀、江、湖之士皆來，編禮著書，日不暇給，夜與之講論經理，亹亹不倦，借鄰寺以處之，朝夕往來，質疑請益如熹時。

translations.literal: Gan then returned home; disciples daily increased; scholars from Ba-Shu and the Jiang and lake regions all came; editing rites and writing books left him no spare day; at night he discussed principle with them, tirelessly earnest; he borrowed a neighboring monastery to lodge them, coming and going morning and evening, questioning and seeking benefit as in Xi's time.
translations.idiomatic: Gan went home; disciples multiplied; scholars from Ba-Shu and the lakes came; he edited rites and wrote books by day and lectured on principle by night without rest, lodging students at a neighboring monastery as in Xi's day.

sentences.zh: 俄命知潮州，辭不行，差主管亳州明道宮，逾月遂乞致仕，詔許之，特授承議郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to administer Chaozhou; he declined and would not go; he was assigned to oversee Mingdao Palace in Bozhou; after a month he begged retirement; the edict granted it and he was specially made Gentlemen for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Chaozhou he declined; assigned to Mingdao Palace in Bozhou, within a month he sought retirement, was granted it, and made Gentlemen for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 既沒後數年，以門人請諡，又特贈朝奉郎，與一子下州文學，諡文肅。

translations.literal: Several years after his death, at his disciples' request for a posthumous title, he was also specially given Recipient of Court Tribute and one son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies; his posthumous title was Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Years after his death disciples sought a posthumous name; he was given Court Tribute and one son lower-prefecture literary studies; posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 有《經解》、文集行於世。

translations.literal: His Exegesis of the Classics and collected writings circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His classical exegesis and collected writings circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 李燔字敬子，南康建昌人。

translations.literal: Li Fan, courtesy name Jingzi, was a man of Jianchang in Nan'kang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, courtesy name Jingzi, was from Jianchang in Nan'kang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依舅氏。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he relied on his mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he lived with his mother's kin.

sentences.zh: 中紹熙元年進士第，授岳州教授，未上，往建陽從朱熹學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed professor at Yuezhou, and before taking up the post went to Jianyang to study under Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he passed the jinshi, was made professor at Yuezhou, and before reporting went to Jianyang to study under Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 熹告以曾子弘毅之語，且曰：「致遠固以毅，而任重貴乎弘也。」

translations.literal: Xi told him Zengzi's words on resolute breadth and said, "To reach far indeed depends on resoluteness, yet to bear heavy burden values breadth all the more."
translations.idiomatic: Xi cited Zengzi on resolute breadth and said, "Distance demands resoluteness, but bearing a heavy charge values breadth more."

sentences.zh: 燔退，以「弘」名其齋而自儆焉。

translations.literal: Fan withdrew and named his study "Breadth" to admonish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fan withdrew and named his study "Breadth" to admonish himself.

sentences.zh: 至岳州，教士以古文六藝，不因時好，且曰：「古之人皆通材，用則文武兼焉。」

translations.literal: At Yuezhou he taught scholars the ancient texts and six arts without following the fashion of the time, and said, "Men of old were all versatile talents; when employed they combined civil and military roles."
translations.idiomatic: At Yuezhou he taught the ancient texts and six arts against fashion and said, "Men of old were versatile; in office they united civil and military skill."

sentences.zh: 即武學諸生文振而識高者拔之，辟射圃，令其習射；

translations.literal: He selected from military-school students those whose writing was strong and understanding keen, opened an archery ground, and had them practice shooting;
translations.idiomatic: He picked keen military students, opened an archery ground, and had them drill;

sentences.zh: 稟老將之長於藝者，以率偷惰。

translations.literal: he reported to veteran generals skilled in the arts to lead the lazy and lax.
translations.idiomatic: he brought in veteran masters of arms to discipline the lax.

sentences.zh: 以祖母卒，解官承重而歸。

translations.literal: When his grandmother died he left office and returned to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother died he left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 改襄陽府教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred to professor at Xiangyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made professor at Xiangyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復往見熹，熹嘉之，凡諸生未達者先令訪燔，俟有所發，乃從熹折衷，諸生畏服。

translations.literal: He again went to see Xi; Xi praised him; any student who had not yet penetrated the teaching was first sent to consult Fan, and only after some opening was he brought to Xi for final judgment; the students submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Xi again; Xi praised him; students not yet clear were sent first to Fan, then to Xi for judgment, and all submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 熹謂人曰：「燔交友有益，而進學可畏，且直諒樸實，處事不苟，它日任斯道者必燔也。」

translations.literal: Xi told others, "Fan's friendships are beneficial and his advance in learning is formidable; moreover he is straightforward, sincere, and plain, and handles affairs without laxity—he who will bear this Way hereafter must be Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Fan's friendships help and his learning awes; he is plain and upright in affairs—he will bear the Way hereafter."

sentences.zh: 熹沒，學禁嚴，燔率同門往會葬，視封窆，不少怵。

translations.literal: When Xi died the ban on the learning was strict; Fan led fellow students to attend the funeral and watched the sealing of the tomb without the least fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died learning was banned; Fan led fellows to the funeral and watched the tomb sealed without fear.

sentences.zh: 及詔訪遺逸，九江守以燔薦，召赴都堂審察，辭，再召，再辭。

translations.literal: When an edict sought hidden worthies, the Jiujiang prefect recommended Fan; he was summoned to the Hall of Court for examination but declined; summoned again, he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought hidden worthies Jiujiang recommended Fan; summoned to court examination he declined, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 郡守請為白鹿書院堂長，學者雲集，講學之盛，它郡無與比。

translations.literal: The prefect asked him to be hall director of White Deer Academy; scholars gathered like clouds; the flourishing of lectures had no peer in other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect made him hall director at White Deer Academy; scholars gathered and lectures flourished beyond any other prefecture.

sentences.zh: 除大理司直，辭，尋添差江西運司幹辦公事，江西帥李珏、漕使王補之交薦之。

translations.literal: He was made director of the Court of Judicial Review but declined; soon he was given additional duty as staff officer of the Jiangxi transport commission; Commander Li Jue and transport commissioner Wang Bu both recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Made judicial review director he declined; soon given additional duty on the Jiangxi transport staff; Li Jue and Wang Bu both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 會洞寇作亂，帥、漕議平之，而各持其說。

translations.literal: When Yao bandits rebelled, commander and transport commissioner debated pacification but each held to his own view.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao bandits rose, commander and transport commissioner debated how to pacify them but disagreed.

sentences.zh: 燔徐曰：「寇非吾民耶？

translations.literal: Fan said slowly, "Are bandits not our people too?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said slowly, "Are bandits not our people as well?

sentences.zh: 豈必皆惡。

translations.literal: Must they all be evil?
translations.idiomatic: Must every one of them be evil?

sentences.zh: 然其如是，誠以吾有司貪刻者激之，及將校之邀功者逼城之耳。

translations.literal: Yet they are as they are truly because our officials' greed and harshness provoked them, and because officers seeking merit pressed the cities.
translations.idiomatic: They are as they are because greedy officials provoked them and officers seeking merit pressed the walls.

sentences.zh: 反是而行之，則皆民矣。」

translations.literal: Do the opposite and they are all people again."
translations.idiomatic: Reverse that and they are people again."

sentences.zh: 帥、漕曰：「幹辦議是。

translations.literal: The commander and transport commissioner said, "The staff officer's plan is right.
translations.idiomatic: Commander and commissioner said, "The staff officer is right.

sentences.zh: 誰可行者？」

translations.literal: Who can go?"
translations.idiomatic: Who can go?"

sentences.zh: 燔請自往，乃駐兵萬安，會近洞諸巡尉，察隅保之尤無良者易置之，分兵守險，馳辯士諭賊逆順禍福，寇皆帖服。

translations.literal: Fan asked to go himself; he then stationed troops at Wan'an, met the patrol officers of nearby Yao caves, observed the worst men in corner guards and replaced them, divided troops to hold defiles, and sent eloquent men to explain fortune and misfortune to the rebels; the bandits all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan volunteered; he stationed troops at Wan'an, met nearby Yao patrol officers, replaced the worst corner guards, held the defiles, sent speakers to explain fortune to the rebels, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 洪州地下，異時贛江漲而堤壞，久雨輒澇，燔白於帥、漕修之，自是田皆沃壤。

translations.literal: Hongzhou lies low; in former times when the Gan River rose the dikes broke and long rains brought floods; Fan reported to commander and transport commissioner to repair them, and thereafter the fields were all fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhou is low-lying; when the Gan rose dikes broke and long rain flooded; Fan had them repaired and fields became fertile.

sentences.zh: 漕司以十四界會子新行，價日損，乃視民稅產物力，各藏會子若干，官為封識，不時點閱，人愛重之則價可增，慢令者黥籍，而民譸張，持空券益不售。

translations.literal: The transport office, because the new fourteen-border huizi notes daily lost value, ordered that according to each household's tax and property a certain number of notes be stored, sealed by the office and inspected from time to time—if people cherished them value might rise; those who disobeyed were tattooed and registered; yet the people clamored and held empty certificates, and the notes sold even less.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office, as new fourteen-border huizi lost value daily, ordered households to hoard sealed notes under inspection—disobedience meant tattooing—yet people clamored with empty certificates and notes sold less.

sentences.zh: 燔與國子學錄李誠之力爭不能止。

translations.literal: Fan and the Guozijian recorder Li Cheng strove together but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Guozijian recorder Li Cheng fought it together but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 燔又入札爭之曰：「錢荒楮涌，子母不足以相權，不能行楮者，由錢不能權之也。

translations.literal: Fan again entered a memorial arguing, "Money is scarce and paper notes flood forth; parent and child cannot balance each other; notes cannot circulate because money cannot balance them.
translations.idiomatic: Fan memorialized again: "Money is scarce and paper floods; parent and child cannot balance; notes fail because money cannot balance them.

sentences.zh: 楮不行而抑民藏之，是棄物也。

translations.literal: If notes do not circulate yet the people are forced to hoard them, that is to discard a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing people to hoard notes that do not circulate is to discard a thing.

sentences.zh: 誠能節用，先穀粟之實務，而不取必於楮幣，則楮幣為實用矣。」

translations.literal: If one can truly economize and put first the solid work of grain, not insisting on paper currency, then paper currency becomes truly useful."
translations.idiomatic: Truly economize, put grain first, do not insist on paper, and paper becomes useful."

sentences.zh: 札入，漕司即弛禁，詣燔謝。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the transport office at once relaxed the ban and came to Fan to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the transport office relaxed the ban and apologized to Fan.

sentences.zh: 燔又念社倉之置，僅貸有田之家，而力田之農不得沾惠，遂倡議裒谷創社倉，以貸佃人。

translations.literal: Fan also reflected that community granaries lent only to households with fields while tenant farmers received no benefit; he therefore proposed gathering grain to found a community granary to lend to tenants.
translations.idiomatic: Fan saw community granaries lent only to landowners while tenants gained nothing; he gathered grain for a granary to lend to tenants.

sentences.zh: 有旨改官，通判潭州，辭，不許。

translations.literal: An edict changed his rank; he was made vice-prefect of Tanzhou; he declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him; made vice-prefect of Tanzhou he declined but was refused.

sentences.zh: 真德秀為長沙帥，一府之事咸咨燔。

translations.literal: When Zhen Dexiu was commander at Changsha, all affairs of the prefecture were consulted with Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen Dexiu commanded Changsha, the whole prefecture consulted Fan.

sentences.zh: 不數月，辭歸。

translations.literal: Within a few months he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 當是時，史彌遠當國，廢皇子竑，燔以三綱所關，自是不復出矣。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Miyuan held the state; he deposed Prince Qi; Fan, because the three bonds were involved, from then on never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Miyuan ruled and deposed Prince Qi, Fan, seeing the three bonds at stake, never went out again.

sentences.zh: 真德秀及右史魏了翁薦之，差權通判隆興府，江西帥魏大有辟充參議官，皆辭，乃以直秘閣主管慶元至道宮。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu and the right historiographer Wei Liaoweng recommended him; he was given acting vice-prefect of Longxing Prefecture; Jiangxi commander Wei Dayou appointed him consulting officer—all declined—and he was finally made direct gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of Zhidao Palace in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng recommended him; acting vice-prefect of Longxing and consulting officer under Wei Dayou he declined; he was made direct gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of Zhidao Palace.

sentences.zh: 燔自惟居閒無以報國，乃薦崔與之、魏了翁、真德秀、陳宓、鄭寅、楊長孺、丁黼、棄宰、龔維藩、徐僑、劉宰、洪咨夔於朝。

translations.literal: Fan reflected that in retirement he had no way to repay the state, and therefore recommended to the court Cui Yuzhi, Wei Liaoweng, Zhen Dexiu, Chen Mi, Zheng Yin, Yang Changru, Ding Fu, Qi Zai, Gong Weifan, Xu Qiao, Liu Zai, and Hong Ziakui.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking he could not repay the state in retirement, Fan recommended Cui Yuzhi, Wei Liaoweng, Zhen Dexiu, Chen Mi, Zheng Yin, Yang Changru, Ding Fu, Qi Zai, Gong Weifan, Xu Qiao, Liu Zai, and Hong Ziakui.

sentences.zh: 紹定五年，帝論及當時高士累召不起者，史臣李心傳以燔對，且曰：「燔乃朱熹高弟，經術行義亞黃榦，當今海內一人而已。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoding the emperor discussed eminent men of the time repeatedly summoned yet refusing to come; the historiographer Li Xinchuan answered with Fan and said, "Fan is a leading disciple of Zhu Xi; in classical learning and conduct he is second only to Huang Gan—within the four seas today there is only this one man."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding year 5 the emperor spoke of eminent men who would not come when summoned; Li Xinchuan answered with Fan: "Fan is Zhu Xi's chief disciple; in learning and conduct he is next to Huang Gan—within the seas there is only this one."

sentences.zh: 帝問今安在，心傳對曰：「燔，南康人，先帝以大理司直召，不起，比乞致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor asked where he was now; Xinchuan answered, "Fan is a man of Nan'kang; the former emperor summoned him as judicial review director and he would not come; recently he has begged retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where Fan was, Xinchuan said, "Fan is from Nan'kang; the former emperor summoned him as judicial review director and he would not come; recently he has begged retirement.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能強起之，以置講筵，其裨聖學豈淺淺哉。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can strongly summon him and place him at the lecture seat, how shallow would the benefit to sagely learning be!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty could summon him to the lecture seat, how shallow would the benefit to sagely learning be!"

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，終不召也。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words but in the end did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed but never summoned him.

sentences.zh: 九江蔡念成稱燔心事有如秋月。

translations.literal: Cai Niancheng of Jiujiang said Fan's inner affairs were like the autumn moon.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Niancheng of Jiujiang said Fan's inner life was like the autumn moon.

sentences.zh: 燔卒，年七十，贈直華文閣，諡文定，補其子舉下州文學。

translations.literal: Fan died at seventy; he was given Direct Gentleman of the Huawen Pavilion and posthumous title Wendi; his son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies.
translations.idiomatic: Fan died at seventy; given Direct Huawen Gentleman and posthumous Wendi; his son received lower-prefecture literary studies.

sentences.zh: 燔嘗曰：「凡人不必待仕宦有位為職事，方為功業，但隨力到處有以及物，即功業矣。」

translations.literal: Fan once said, "A man need not wait until he holds office and rank to have a duty; wherever his strength reaches and he can reach others, that is achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Fan once said, "One need not wait for office to have achievement; wherever strength reaches to help others, that is achievement."

sentences.zh: 又嘗曰：「仕宦至卿相，不可失寒素體。

translations.literal: He also said, "In office up to minister and counselor one must not lose the plain body of cold and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Even as minister one must not lose plain simplicity.

sentences.zh: 夫子無入不自得者，正以磨挫驕奢，不至居移氣、養移體。」

translations.literal: The Master's being at ease wherever he entered was precisely to grind down pride and luxury so that dwelling would not shift the temper nor nurture shift the body."
translations.idiomatic: The Master's ease wherever he entered was to grind pride and luxury so dwelling would not shift temper nor nurture shift the body."

sentences.zh: 因誦古語曰：「分之所在，一毫躋攀不上，善處者退一步耳。」

translations.literal: He therefore quoted an old saying: "Where rank lies, not a hair's breadth may one climb up; the wise man steps back a pace."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted an old saying: "Where rank sits, not a hair may one climb; the wise step back."

sentences.zh: 故燔處貧賤患難若平素，不為動，被服布素，雖貴不易。

translations.literal: Therefore Fan in poverty, baseness, and hardship was as in ordinary times and was not moved; he wore plain cloth and would not change it though honored.
translations.idiomatic: Fan in poverty and hardship was unmoved as in ordinary times and wore plain cloth though honored.

sentences.zh: 入仕凡四十二年，而歷官不過七考。

translations.literal: He entered office for forty-two years yet held office through no more than seven evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: In forty-two years of service he passed no more than seven evaluations.

sentences.zh: 居家講道，學者宗之，與黃榦並稱曰「黃、李。」

translations.literal: At home he lectured on the Way; scholars took him as their model; with Huang Gan he was jointly called "Huang and Li."
translations.idiomatic: At home he taught the Way; scholars honored him; with Huang Gan he was called Huang and Li."

sentences.zh: 孫鑣，登進士第。

translations.literal: His grandson Biao passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Biao passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 張洽字元德，臨江之清江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qia, courtesy name Yuande, was a man of Qingjiang in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qia, courtesy name Yuande, was from Qingjiang in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 父紱，第進士。

translations.literal: His father Fu passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 洽少穎異，從朱熹學，自《六經》傳注而下，皆究其指歸，至於諸子百家、山經地誌、老子浮屠之說，無所不讀。

translations.literal: Qia was precocious in youth and studied under Zhu Xi; from the Six Classics and their commentaries downward he traced all to their ends; as for the hundred schools, mountain classics, geographical records, Laozi, and Buddhist teachings, there was nothing he did not read.
translations.idiomatic: Qia was precocious and studied under Zhu Xi; from the Six Classics down he traced every teaching; he read the hundred schools, geographies, Laozi, and Buddhist texts without exception.

sentences.zh: 嘗取管子所謂「思之思之，又重思之，思之不通，鬼神將通之」之語，以為窮理之要。

translations.literal: He once took Guanzi's words "Think, think; think again and weigh; if thinking does not penetrate, spirits will penetrate" as the key to exhausting principle.
translations.idiomatic: He took Guanzi's "Think, think; think again; if thought fails, spirits will aid" as the key to exhausting principle.

sentences.zh: 熹嘉其篤志，謂黃榦曰：「所望以永斯道之傳，如二三君者不數人也。」

translations.literal: Xi praised his earnest will and said to Huang Gan, "The hope to perpetuate this Way's transmission—men like these two or three are not many."
translations.idiomatic: Xi praised his resolve and told Huang Gan, "Those who will perpetuate the Way—such men are few."

sentences.zh: 時行社倉法，洽請於縣，貸常平米三百石，建倉里中，六年而歸其本於官，鄉人利之。

translations.literal: When the community-granary law was in force, Qia asked the county to lend three hundred piculs of ever-normal grain, built a granary in the village, and after six years returned the principal to the office; the villagers profited.
translations.idiomatic: When community granaries were enacted Qia borrowed three hundred piculs of ever-normal grain, built a village granary, returned principal in six years, and villagers profited.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年中第，授松滋尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading he passed the examination and was appointed sheriff of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading he passed and was made sheriff of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 湖右經界不正，弊日甚，洽請行推排法，令以委洽。

translations.literal: Land boundaries on the right of the lake were incorrect and abuses daily worsened; Qia asked to carry out the push-and-check method and the prefecture entrusted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lake-right land boundaries were wrong and abuses grew; Qia carried out push-and-check and the prefecture entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 洽於是令民自實其土地疆界產業之數投於匱，乃籌核而次第之，吏奸無所匿。

translations.literal: He then had the people themselves report the numbers of their land boundaries and property into a chest; he calculated and ranked them in order, and clerical fraud had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He had people report land and property into a chest, calculated and ranked them, and clerical fraud could not hide.

sentences.zh: 其後十餘年，訟者猶援以為證云。

translations.literal: More than ten years later litigants still cited it as proof.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later litigants still cited it as proof.

sentences.zh: 改袁州司理參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial military adjutant of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judicial military adjutant of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 有大囚，訊之則服，尋復變異，且力能動搖官吏，累年不決，而逮系者甚眾。

translations.literal: There was a great prisoner who confessed under questioning, then again changed his story, and could moreover sway officials; for many years it was not decided while those detained were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: A great prisoner confessed then changed his tale and swayed officials; for years it was unresolved while many remained detained.

sentences.zh: 洽以白提點刑獄，殺之。

translations.literal: Qia reported to the judicial intendant and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qia reported to the judicial intendant and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 有盜黠甚，辭不能折。

translations.literal: There was a very cunning thief whose words he could not refute.
translations.idiomatic: A very cunning thief defied his questioning.

sentences.zh: 會獄有兄弟爭財者，洽諭之曰：「訟於官，祗為胥吏之地，且冒法以求勝，孰與各守分以全手足之愛乎？」

translations.literal: When brothers in another case disputed property, Qia admonished them, "To sue at court is only to make a place for clerks; moreover you risk law to win—why not each keep his share and preserve brotherly love?"
translations.idiomatic: When brothers disputed property Qia said, "Court is only clerks' ground; risking law to win—why not keep your shares and preserve brotherly love?"

sentences.zh: 辭氣懇切，訟者感悟。

translations.literal: His words were earnest and the litigants were moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was earnest and the litigants were moved.

sentences.zh: 盜聞之，自伏。

translations.literal: The thief heard it and confessed of himself.
translations.idiomatic: The thief heard and confessed.

sentences.zh: 民有殺人，賄其子焚之，居數年，事敗，洽治其獄無狀，憂之，且白郡委官體訪。

translations.literal: A man killed someone and bribed his son to burn the body; after several years the affair was exposed; Qia tried the case without finding proof, was troubled, and reported to the prefecture to commission an on-site inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: A killer bribed his son to burn the corpse; years later it was exposed; Qia found no proof, worried, and asked the prefect to investigate on site.

sentences.zh: 俄夢有人拜於庭，示以傷痕在脅。

translations.literal: Soon he dreamed of someone bowing in the court and showing wounds on the ribs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he dreamed of someone bowing in court showing rib wounds.

sentences.zh: 翌日，委官上其事，果然。

translations.literal: The next day the commissioned officer reported the matter, and it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the officer reported, and it was so.

sentences.zh: 郡守以倉稟虛，籍倉吏二十餘家，命洽鞫之，洽廉知為都吏所賣。

translations.literal: The prefect, because the granary stores were empty, registered more than twenty granary households and ordered Qia to try them; Qia clearly knew they had been sold out by the chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect, finding granaries empty, registered twenty granary households and ordered Qia to try them; Qia knew the chief clerk had framed them.

sentences.zh: 都吏者，州之巨蠹也，嘗干於倉不獲，故以此中之。

translations.literal: The chief clerk was the prefecture's great parasite; he had once tried the granary without success and therefore struck at them this way.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk was the prefecture's great parasite; refused at the granary, he framed these men.

sentences.zh: 洽度守意銳未可嬰，姑繫之，而密令計倉庾所入以白守曰：「君之籍二十餘家者，以胥吏也。

translations.literal: Qia judged the prefect's mind was sharp and not to be provoked yet, and for the time being detained him while secretly ordering a count of granary intake to report to the prefect, "The more than twenty households Your Lordship registered are because of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Qia saw the prefect was sharp and not to be crossed; he detained the clerk and secretly counted intake, telling the prefect, "Your twenty households are because of clerks.

sentences.zh: 今校數歲之中所入，已豐於昔，由是觀之，胥吏妄矣。

translations.literal: Now comparing intake over several years, it is already richer than before; viewed thus, the clerks lied.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing years of intake, stores are richer than before—the clerks lied.

sentences.zh: 君必不忍受胥吏之妄，而籍無罪之家也。

translations.literal: Your Lordship surely cannot bear clerks' lies yet register innocent households.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot bear clerks' lies yet register innocent households.

sentences.zh: 若以罪胥吏，過乃可免。」

translations.literal: If you punish the clerks, the fault may be escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Punish the clerks and the fault is escaped."

sentences.zh: 守悟，為罷都吏，而免所籍之家。

translations.literal: The prefect understood, dismissed the chief clerk, and released the registered households.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect understood, dismissed the chief clerk, and released the households.

sentences.zh: 知永新縣。

translations.literal: He was made magistrate of Yongxin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 一日謁告，聞獄中榜笞聲，蓋獄吏受賕，乘間訊囚使誣服也。

translations.literal: One day on leave he heard the sound of beating in the prison; it was the jailer who had taken a bribe and seized an interval to examine a prisoner and make him confess falsely.
translations.idiomatic: On leave he heard beating in the prison—a jailer had taken a bribe and forced a false confession.

sentences.zh: 洽大怒，亟執付獄，明日以上於郡，黥之。

translations.literal: Qia was greatly angered, immediately seized him and put him in prison; the next day he reported upward to the prefecture and had him tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Qia in rage seized him, jailed him, and next day reported to the prefecture for tattooing.

sentences.zh: 湖南酃寇作亂，與縣接壤，民大恐。

translations.literal: Hunan Ling bandits rebelled; the county bordered them and the people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ling bandits rebelled in Hunan; the county bordered them and people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 洽單車以往，邑佐、寓士交諫，弗聽。

translations.literal: Qia went alone in a single cart; county assistants and resident gentlemen all urged him together but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qia went alone in a single cart; aides and resident gentry urged him in turn but he would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 至則寇未嘗至，乃延見隅官，訪利害而犒之，因行安福境上，結約土豪，得其歡心。

translations.literal: When he arrived the bandits had not yet come; he then received the corner officers, inquired into gains and losses and rewarded them, and traveling the border of Anfu made covenants with local strongmen and won their goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived before the bandits; he received corner officers, asked their needs, rewarded them, toured the Anfu border, made covenants with local strongmen, and won their hearts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南安舒寇將犯境，聞有備，乃去。

translations.literal: Before long Shu's bandits in Nan'an were about to invade the border; hearing there were preparations, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nan'an Shu bandits were about to invade; hearing defenses were ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以江東提舉常平薦，通判池州。

translations.literal: On recommendation of the Jiangdong intendant for ever-normal granaries, he was made vice-prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by the Jiangdong ever-normal intendant, he became vice-prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 獄有張德修者，誤蹴人以死，獄吏誣以故殺，洽訊而疑之，請再鞫，守不聽。

translations.literal: In prison was Zhang Dexiu, who by mistake kicked a man to death; the jailer charged intentional killing; Qia questioned him and doubted it, asking to retry the case, but the prefect would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiu in prison had kicked a man to death by mistake; the jailer charged murder; Qia doubted it and asked a retrial; the prefect refused.

sentences.zh: 會提點常平袁甫至，時方大旱，禱不應，洽言於甫曰：「漢、晉以來，濫刑而致旱，伸冤而得雨，載於方冊可考也。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Fu, intendant for ever-normal granaries, arrived; there was great drought and prayers did not answer; Qia said to Fu, "Since Han and Jin, excessive punishment has brought drought and righting wrongs has brought rain—this is recorded in books and can be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-normal intendant Yuan Fu arrived in great drought; prayers failed; Qia told Fu, "Since Han and Jin, harsh punishment brought drought and righting wrongs brought rain—books record it.

sentences.zh: 今天大旱，焉知非由德修事乎？」

translations.literal: Today the sky is greatly dry—how do we know it is not because of the Dexiu affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Today drought is severe—who knows it is not the Dexiu case?"

sentences.zh: 甫為閱款狀於獄，德修遂從徒罪。

translations.literal: Fu reviewed the case papers in prison and Dexiu was then sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reviewed the prison papers and Dexiu received penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 復白郡請蠲征稅，寬催科，以召和氣，守為寬稅。

translations.literal: Qia again reported to the prefecture asking to cancel levies and ease collection to summon harmonious qi; the prefect eased taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Qia asked the prefect to cancel levies and ease collection to summon harmony; the prefect eased taxes.

sentences.zh: 三日果大雨，民甚悅。

translations.literal: Three days later great rain indeed fell and the people were very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later rain fell and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 洽數以病請祠，至是主管建昌仙都觀，以慶壽恩賜緋衣、銀魚。

translations.literal: Qia several times begged a sinecure on grounds of illness; now he was made custodian of Xiandu Abbey in Jianchang and by the Celebrating Longevity grace was given crimson robe and silver fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Qia had often begged a sinecure for illness; now he kept Xiandu Abbey in Jianchang and received crimson robe and silver fish by Celebrating Longevity grace.

sentences.zh: 時袁甫提點江東刑獄，甫以白鹿書院廢弛，招洽為長。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Fu was judicial intendant of Jiangdong; seeing White Deer Academy neglected, he invited Qia to be its director.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu was Jiangdong judicial intendant; finding White Deer Academy neglected, he made Qia director.

sentences.zh: 洽曰：「嘻，是先師之跡也，其可辭！」

translations.literal: Qia said, "Alas—that is my former teacher's trace; how can I decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Qia said, "That is my teacher's place—how can I refuse!"

sentences.zh: 至則選好學之士日與講說，而汰其不率教者。

translations.literal: When he arrived he chose eager learners to lecture daily and removed those who would not follow instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He chose keen students for daily lectures and removed the unruly.

sentences.zh: 凡養士之田乾沒於豪右者復之。

translations.literal: All fields supporting students that had been swallowed by powerful families he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered student-support fields seized by powerful families.

sentences.zh: 學興，即謝病去。

translations.literal: When learning flourished he at once resigned on grounds of illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the academy flourished he resigned on illness and left.

sentences.zh: 端平初，大臣多薦洽，召赴都堂審察，洽以疾不赴，乃除秘書郎，尋遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping many great ministers recommended Qia; he was summoned to court examination but would not go on grounds of illness; he was then made secretary and soon promoted assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At Duanping's start ministers recommended Qia; summoned to court examination he stayed home for illness; made secretary then assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 度正、葉味道在經幄，帝數問張洽何時可到，將以說書待洽，洽固辭，遂除直秘閣，主管建康崇禧觀。

translations.literal: Du Zheng and Ye Weidao were in the classics mat; the emperor several times asked when Zhang Qia could arrive, intending to make him expositor; Qia firmly declined and was finally made direct gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of Chongxi Abbey in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng and Ye Weidao served the classics mat; the emperor asked when Qia would come to make him expositor; Qia declined and was made direct gentleman keeping Chongxi Abbey in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，以疾乞致仕，十月卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi he begged retirement on grounds of illness; in the tenth month he died at seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaxi he sought retirement for illness; in the tenth month he died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 洽自少用力於敬，故以「主一」名齋。

translations.literal: From youth Qia applied effort to reverence and therefore named his study "Maintaining Oneness."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he worked at reverence and named his study "Maintaining Oneness."

sentences.zh: 平居不異常人，至義所當為，則勇不可奪。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was no different from other men, but where righteousness required action his courage could not be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he seemed ordinary, but where duty called his courage could not be shaken.

sentences.zh: 居閒不言朝廷事，或因災異變故，輒顰蹙不樂，及聞一君子進用，士大夫直言朝廷得失，則喜見顏色。

translations.literal: In retirement he did not speak of court affairs, yet when disaster or change occurred he would knit his brows unhappily; when he heard a worthy man advanced or gentlemen speak frankly of court right and wrong, joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Retired he did not discuss court affairs, yet disasters wrung his brow; when a worthy was advanced or gentlemen spoke frankly of court errors, joy showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 所交皆名士，如呂祖儉、黃榦、趙崇憲、蔡淵、吳必大、輔廣、李道傳、李燔、葉味道、李閎祖、李方子、柴中行、真德秀、魏了翁、李埴、趙汝讜、陳貴誼、杜孝嚴、度正、張嗣古，皆敬慕之。

translations.literal: Those he associated with were all famous men, such as Lü Zujian, Huang Gan, Zhao Chongxian, Cai Yuan, Wu Bida, Fu Guang, Li Daochuan, Li Fan, Ye Weidao, Li Hongzu, Li Fangzi, Chai Zhongxing, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Li Qi, Zhao Rujing, Chen Guiyi, Du Xiaoyan, Du Zheng, and Zhang Sigu—all revered him.
translations.idiomatic: His friends were famous men—Lü Zujian, Huang Gan, Zhao Chongxian, Cai Yuan, Wu Bida, Fu Guang, Li Daochuan, Li Fan, Ye Weidao, Li Hongzu, Li Fangzi, Chai Zhongxing, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Li Qi, Zhao Rujing, Chen Guiyi, Du Xiaoyan, Du Zheng, Zhang Sigu—all revered him.

sentences.zh: 卒後一日，有旨除直寶章閣。

translations.literal: One day after his death an edict appointed him Direct Gentleman of the Baozhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A day after his death an edict made him Direct Baozhang Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《春秋集注》、《春秋集傳》、《左氏蒙求》、《續通鑒長編事略》、《歷代郡縣地理沿革表》、文集。

translations.literal: His writings include Collected Notes on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Collected Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, A Primer for the Zuo Tradition, Outline of Events in the Continued Comprehensive Mirror, Tables of Commandery and County Geography Through the Ages, and collected works.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Notes on the Spring and Autumn, Collected Commentary, Zuo Tradition Primer, Outline of the Continued Mirror, geographical tables through the ages, and collected works.

sentences.zh: 子㯝、檉，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: His sons Kan and Cheng were granted jinshi by special grace.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kan and Cheng received jinshi by special grace.

sentences.zh: 陳淳字安卿，漳州龍溪人。

translations.literal: Chen Chun, courtesy name Anqing, was a man of Longxi in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chun, courtesy name Anqing, was from Longxi in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少習舉子業，林宗臣見而奇之，且曰：「此非聖賢事業也。」

translations.literal: In youth he studied for the examinations; Lin Zongchen saw him and marveled, saying, "This is not the enterprise of sages and worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Young he studied for examinations; Lin Zongchen marveled and said, "This is not the work of sages."

sentences.zh: 因授以《近思錄》，淳退而讀之，遂盡棄其業焉。

translations.literal: He therefore gave him Reflections on Things Near at Hand; Chun withdrew and read it and thereupon wholly abandoned that pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him Reflections on Things Near at Hand; Chun read it and abandoned examination studies.

sentences.zh: 及朱熹來守其鄉，淳請受教，熹曰：「凡閱義理，必窮其原，如為人父何故止於慈，為人子何故止於孝，其他可類推也。」

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi came to administer his district, Chun asked to receive instruction; Xi said, "Whenever you examine principle you must exhaust its root—as when one is father, why does one stop at kindness, when one is son, why at filial piety; the rest may be inferred by kind."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi governed his district Chun sought instruction; Xi said, "In examining principle exhaust its root—why does fatherhood stop at kindness, sonhood at filial piety; infer the rest by kind."

sentences.zh: 淳聞而為學益力，日求其所未至。

translations.literal: Chun heard this and pressed his learning harder, daily seeking what he had not yet reached.
translations.idiomatic: Chun pressed harder and daily sought what he had not reached.

sentences.zh: 熹數語人以「南來，吾道喜得陳淳」，門人有疑問不合者，則稱淳善問。

translations.literal: Xi often told people, "Coming south, my Way is glad to have gained Chen Chun"; when disciples had doubts that would not agree he called Chun good at questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Xi often told people, "Coming south, I am glad to have gained Chen Chun"; when students disagreed he called Chun good at questions.

sentences.zh: 後十年，淳復往見熹，陳其所得，時熹已寢疾，語之曰：「如公所學，已見本原，所闕者下學之功爾。」

translations.literal: Ten years later Chun again went to see Xi and presented his attainments; Xi was already gravely ill and said to him, "As you have learned, you have seen the root; what you lack is the work of lower learning."
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later Chun presented his attainments; Xi was gravely ill and said, "You have seen the root; what lacks is lower learning."

sentences.zh: 自是所聞皆要切語，凡三月而熹卒。

translations.literal: From then on what he heard were all essential words; in three months Xi died.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he heard only essential words; in three months Xi died.

sentences.zh: 淳追思師訓，前自裁抑，無書不讀，無物不格，日積月累，義理貫通，洞見條緒。

translations.literal: Chun recalled his teacher's instruction and beforehand restrained himself; no book he did not read, no thing he did not investigate; month by month principle ran through and threads were clear.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling his teacher he restrained himself, read all books, investigated all things, and month by month principle ran clear.

sentences.zh: 故其言太極曰：「太極只是理，理本圓，故太極之體渾淪。

translations.literal: Thus he said of the Supreme Ultimate: "The Supreme Ultimate is only principle; principle is originally round, and therefore the substance of the Supreme Ultimate is undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: On the Supreme Ultimate he said: "It is only principle; principle is round, so its substance is undifferentiated.

sentences.zh: 以理言，則自末而本，自本而末，一聚一散，而太極無所不極其至。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of principle, from the branch to the root and from the root to the branch, gathering and scattering, the Supreme Ultimate reaches its utmost everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In principle, from branch to root and root to branch, gathering and scattering, the Supreme Ultimate reaches everywhere.

sentences.zh: 自萬古之前與萬古之後，無端無始，此渾淪太極之全體也。

translations.literal: From endless ages before to endless ages after, without beginning or end—this is the whole undifferentiated body of the Supreme Ultimate.
