translations.idiomatic: From endless past to endless future without beginning or end—this is the whole undifferentiated Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 自其沖漠無朕，而天地萬物皆由是出，及天地萬物既由是出，又復沖漠無朕，此渾淪無極之妙用也。

translations.literal: From its still emptiness heaven, earth, and the myriad things all emerge; once heaven, earth, and the myriad things have emerged, it again returns to still emptiness—this is the wondrous function of undifferentiated limitlessness.
translations.idiomatic: From still emptiness all things emerge; once emerged it returns to still emptiness—the wondrous function of the limitless.

sentences.zh: 聖人一心渾淪太極之全體，而酬酢萬變，無非太極流行之用。

translations.literal: The sage's one mind is the whole undifferentiated body of the Supreme Ultimate, and in responding to myriad changes nothing is not the circulating function of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's one mind is the whole undifferentiated Supreme Ultimate; responding to change is all its circulating function.

sentences.zh: 學問工夫，須從萬事萬物中貫過，湊成一渾淪大本，又於渾淪大本中散為萬事萬物，使無少窒礙，然後實體得渾淪至極者在我，而大用不差矣。」

translations.literal: The effort of learning must run through the myriad things and affairs of the world and gather into one undifferentiated great root; then within that great root scatter again into myriad things and affairs so that nothing is obstructed—only then does the undifferentiated utmost substance dwell in oneself and the great function is not in error."
translations.idiomatic: Learning must run through all things and gather one undifferentiated root, then scatter again without obstruction—then the utmost substance is in oneself and the great function is true."

sentences.zh: 其言仁曰：「仁只是天理生生之全體，無表裡、動靜、隱顯、精粗之間，惟此心純是天理之公，而絕無一毫人欲之私，乃可以當其名。

translations.literal: On benevolence he said: "Benevolence is only the whole living body of heaven's principle generating and generating, without interval between outer and inner, movement and stillness, hidden and manifest, coarse and fine; only when this mind is purely the public of heaven's principle and absolutely without a hair of human desire's privacy can it bear the name.
translations.idiomatic: On benevolence: "Benevolence is heaven's principle wholly alive, without gap between inner and outer, movement and stillness; only when the mind is purely heaven's public without human desire can it bear the name.

sentences.zh: 若一處有病痛，一事有欠闕，一念有間斷，則私意行而生理息，即頑痹不仁矣。」

translations.literal: If in one place there is pain, in one affair there is lack, in one thought there is break, then private intent acts and living principle ceases—that is benumbed unbenevolence."
translations.idiomatic: One pain, one lack, one broken thought—and private intent runs while living principle stops: that is benumbed unbenevolence."

sentences.zh: 其語學者曰：「道理初無玄妙，只在日用人事間，但循序用功，便自有見。

translations.literal: To learners he said: "Principle at first has no mystery; it is only in daily human affairs; just apply effort in order and you will naturally see.
translations.idiomatic: He told learners: "Principle is not mysterious; it is in daily affairs; apply effort in order and you will see.

sentences.zh: 所謂『下學上達』者，須下學工夫到，乃可從事上達，然不可以此而安於小成也。

translations.literal: What is called 'lower learning reaching upward' requires lower learning's effort to be complete before one can work at upward reaching—yet one cannot rest content with small accomplishment on that account."
translations.idiomatic: Lower learning reaching upward' needs lower learning complete before upward work—but do not rest in small accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 夫盈天地間千條萬緒，是多少人事；

translations.literal: Filling heaven and earth are thousands upon thousands of threads—how many are human affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Filling heaven and earth are thousands of threads—how many human affairs;

sentences.zh: 聖人大成之地，千節萬目，是多少功夫。

translations.literal: the sage's ground of great completion has thousands of joints and ten thousand eyes—how much effort is that.
translations.idiomatic: the sage's ground of great completion has thousands of joints and myriad facets—how much effort.

sentences.zh: 惟當開拓心胸，大作基址。

translations.literal: One must only open the mind and breast and make a great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: One must open the mind and lay a great foundation.

sentences.zh: 須萬理明徹於胸中，將此心放在天地間一例看，然後可以語孔、孟之樂。

translations.literal: Myriad principles must be clear in the breast; place this mind in the world as one case, and only then can one speak of the joy of Confucius and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad principles must be clear in the breast; view the mind as one with the world—then one may speak of Confucius and Mencius's joy.

sentences.zh: 須明三代法度，通之於當今而無不宜，然後為全儒，而可以語王佐事業。

translations.literal: One must understand the institutions of the Three Dynasties and run them through the present without inappropriateness—only then is one a complete Confucian and can speak of king-assisting enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Understand Three Dynasties institutions and apply them to the present—then one is a complete Confucian fit for king-assisting work.

sentences.zh: 須運用酬酢，如探諸囊中而不匱，然後為資之深，取之左右逢其原，而真為已物矣。

translations.literal: One must deploy and respond as if probing the bag without exhaustion—only then is one's store deep, taking from left and right one meets the source, and it is truly one's own.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy and respond as from an inexhaustible bag—then the store is deep, left and right meet the source, and it is truly one's own.

sentences.zh: 至於以天理人欲分數而驗賓主進退之幾，如好好色，惡惡臭，而為天理人欲強弱之證，必使之於是是非非如辨黑白，如遇鏌鎁，不容有騎牆不決之疑，則雖艱難險阻之中，無不從容自適，夫然後為知之至而行之盡。」

translations.literal: As for dividing heaven's principle and human desire by proportion to test the several of guest and host, advance and retreat—as in loving beauty and hating stench, making proof of the relative strength of principle and desire—one must make yes and no, right and wrong, as clear as black and white; as when meeting a sword edge, no room for straddling indecision; then even amid hardship and danger one is everywhere at ease—only then is knowing utmost and action complete."
translations.idiomatic: Divide principle and desire, test advance and retreat as loving beauty and hating stench—yes and no must be black and white, no straddling; then even in danger one is at ease: knowing is utmost and action complete."

sentences.zh: 此語又中學者膏肓，而示以標的也。

translations.literal: This speech again struck the learners' deep sickness and showed them the target.
translations.idiomatic: This speech struck learners' deep sickness and showed the target.

sentences.zh: 淳性孝，母疾亟，號泣於天，乞以身代。

translations.literal: Chun was filial by nature; when his mother's illness was critical he wept to heaven and begged to substitute his body.
translations.idiomatic: Filial by nature, when his mother was critical he wept to heaven and begged to take her place.

sentences.zh: 弟妹未有室家者，皆婚嫁之。

translations.literal: Younger brothers and sisters who had not yet married he all married off.
translations.idiomatic: He married off brothers and sisters not yet wed.

sentences.zh: 葬宗族之喪無歸者。

translations.literal: He buried clansmen whose funerals had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: He buried clansmen with nowhere to bury their dead.

sentences.zh: 居鄉不沽名徇俗，恬然退守，若無聞焉。

translations.literal: In the village he did not chase fame or follow fashion, but calmly guarded withdrawal as if unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: In the village he did not chase fame but calmly withdrew as if unknown.

sentences.zh: 然名播天下，世雖不用，而憂時論事，感慨動人，郡守以下皆禮重之，時造其廬而請焉。

translations.literal: Yet his name spread under heaven; though the age did not employ him, when he discussed the times and affairs his feeling moved people; prefects and below all honored him and at times came to his hut to ask.
translations.idiomatic: His name spread worldwide; though unused, his talk of the times moved people; prefects honored him and came to his hut.

sentences.zh: 嘉定九年，待試中都，歸過嚴陵郡守鄭之悌，率僚屬延講郡庠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiading, awaiting examination in the capital, returning he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie led staff to extend him at the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 9, awaiting capital examination, he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie and staff heard him lecture at the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 淳嘆陸、張、王，學問無源，全用禪家宗旨，認形氣之虛靈知覺為天理之妙，不由窮理格物，而欲徑造上達之境，反托聖門以自標榜。

translations.literal: Chun sighed over Lu, Zhang, and Wang: their learning had no source and wholly used Chanist aims, taking the void spirit and knowing awareness of form and qi as the wonder of heaven's principle, not by exhausting principle and investigating things yet wishing to reach upward directly, and in reverse borrowing the sage's gate to set up their signboard.
translations.idiomatic: Chun lamented Lu, Zhang, and Wang: learning without source, using Chan aims, taking void spirit and awareness as heaven's principle, skipping investigation yet claiming the sage's gate.

sentences.zh: 遂發明吾道之體統，師友之淵源，用功之節目，讀書之次序，為四章以示學者。

translations.literal: He then set forth the substance of our Way, the deep source of teacher and friend, the nodes of effort, and the order of reading in four chapters to show learners.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth our Way's substance, teachers' source, effort's nodes, and reading's order in four chapters for learners.

sentences.zh: 明年，以特奏恩授迪功郎、泉州安溪主簿，未上而沒，年六十五。

translations.literal: The next year by special memorial grace he was made probationary merit officer and recorder of Anxi in Quanzhou; before reporting he died at sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Next year by special grace he was made probationary merit officer and Anxi recorder in Quanzhou; before reporting he died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 其所著有《語孟大學中庸》口義、字義、詳講，《禮》、《詩》、《女學》等書，門人錄其語，號《筠谷瀨口金山所聞》。

translations.literal: His writings include oral exegeses and character meanings with detailed commentary on the Analects, Mencius, Great Learning, and Doctrine of the Mean, and books on Rites, Odes, and Women's Learning; disciples recorded his words as What Was Heard at Jun Valley, Lai Mouth, and Jin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote oral exegeses on the Four Books, Rites, Odes, and Women's Learning; disciples recorded What Was Heard at Jun Valley, Lai Mouth, and Jin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 李方子

translations.literal: Li Fangzi
translations.idiomatic: Li Fangzi

sentences.zh: 李方子字公晦，昭武人。

translations.literal: Li Fangzi, courtesy name Gonghui, was a man of Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fangzi, courtesy name Gonghui, was from Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 少博學能文，為人端謹純篤。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly learned and skilled at writing; as a man he was proper, cautious, pure, and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Young he was learned and wrote well; proper, cautious, pure, and earnest.

sentences.zh: 初見朱熹，謂曰：「觀公為人，自是寡過，但寬大中要規矩，和緩中要果決。」

translations.literal: When he first met Zhu Xi, Xi said to him, "Seeing you as a man, you are naturally free of many faults—but within breadth and tolerance there must be rule, and within gentleness and ease there must be firm decision."
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Zhu Xi, Xi said, "You are naturally free of many faults—but breadth needs rule and gentleness needs firm decision."

sentences.zh: 遂以「果」名齋。

translations.literal: He thereupon named his study "Fruit."
translations.idiomatic: He named his study "Fruit."

sentences.zh: 長游太學，學官李道傳折官位輩行具刺就謁。

translations.literal: Growing up he traveled the Imperial College; the academic officer Li Daochuan folded rank and generation and with calling cards came to visit.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial College, academic officer Li Daochuan set aside rank and came with calling cards.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，廷對擢第三，調泉州觀察推官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading, in the palace examination he was placed third and was appointed investigating and pushing officer of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 7 he placed third in the palace exam and was made Quanzhou investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 適真德秀來為守，以師友禮之，郡政大小咸咨焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhen Dexiu came as prefect and treated him with teacher-friend ceremony; great and small prefectural affairs were all consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu came as prefect and treated him as teacher and friend; all prefectural affairs were consulted.

sentences.zh: 暇則辨論經訓，至夜分不倦。

translations.literal: In leisure they debated classical exegesis until midnight without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure they debated classics until midnight without tiring.

sentences.zh: 故事，秩滿必先通書廟堂乃除，方子曰：「以書通，是求也。」

translations.literal: By precedent, when rank expired one must first notify the temple hall by letter before promotion; Fangzi said, "To notify by letter is to beg."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent one must write the temple before promotion; Fangzi said, "Writing the temple is begging."

sentences.zh: 時丞相彌遠聞之怒，逾年始除國子錄。

translations.literal: Chief minister Miyuan heard this and was angry; after more than a year he was finally made Guozijian recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Miyuan was angry; after a year he was made Guozijian recorder.

sentences.zh: 無何，將選入宮僚，而方子不少貶以求合。

translations.literal: Before long he was to be chosen for palace staff, yet Fangzi would not slightly demean himself to fit in.
translations.idiomatic: Soon to be chosen for palace staff, Fangzi would not demean himself to fit in.

sentences.zh: 或告彌遠曰：「此真德秀黨也。」

translations.literal: Someone told Miyuan, "This is truly Zhen Dexiu's faction."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Miyuan, "He is Zhen Dexiu's man."

sentences.zh: 使臺臣劾罷之。

translations.literal: He had censorial officials impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 方子既歸，學者畢集，危坐竟日，未始傾側，對賓客一語不妄發，雖奴隸亦不加詬詈，然常嚴憚之。

translations.literal: After Fangzi returned, learners all gathered; he sat upright all day without leaning; facing guests he did not speak a careless word; even slaves he did not revile, yet they always feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Returned, learners gathered; he sat upright all day; with guests he spoke no careless word; even slaves he did not revile yet they feared him.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「吾於問學雖未能周盡，然幸於大本有見處，此心常覺泰然，不為物欲所漬爾。」

translations.literal: He once told others, "In questioning learning I have not yet been thorough, yet fortunately on the great root I have a place of insight; this mind is often calm and is not soaked by material desire."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Though not thorough in learning, on the great root I have insight; this mind stays calm and is not soaked by desire."

sentences.zh: 其亡也，天子閔之，與一子恩澤。

translations.literal: At his death the Son of Heaven pitied him and granted favor to one son.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor pitied him and favored one son.

sentences.zh: 黃灝字商伯，南康都昌人。

translations.literal: Huang Hao, courtesy name Shangbo, was a man of Duchang in Nan'kang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao, courtesy name Shangbo, was from Duchang in Nan'kang.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟強記，肄業荊山僧舍三年，入太學，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen, understanding, and strong in memory; he studied three years at a Jingshan monastery, entered the Imperial College, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Young he was keen and memorized well; three years at Jingshan monastery, then the college and jinshi.

sentences.zh: 教授隆興府，知德化縣，以興學校、崇政化為本。

translations.literal: Professor at Longxing Prefecture, magistrate of Dehua County—he took founding schools and honoring good government as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Professor at Longxing and magistrate of Dehua—he rooted work in schools and good government.

sentences.zh: 歲饉，行振給有方。

translations.literal: In a famine year he carried out relief with method.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he relieved with method.

sentences.zh: 王藺、劉穎薦於朝，除登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: Wang Lin and Liu Ying recommended him to court and he was made officer of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin and Liu Ying recommended him; he was made Petition Drum Court officer.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，遷太常寺簿，論今禮教廢闕，請敕有司取政和冠昏喪葬儀，及司馬光、高閌等書參訂行之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne he was moved to recorder of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized that ritual teaching was now abandoned and asked the relevant offices to take the Zhenghe crown, wedding, mourning, and burial rites and books by Sima Guang, Gao Min, and others, revise and enact them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong made him Imperial Sacrifices recorder; he said ritual teaching was abandoned and asked offices to revise Zhenghe rites and books by Sima Guang and Gao Min and enact them.

sentences.zh: 除太府寺丞，出知常州，提舉本路常平。

translations.literal: Made vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, he went out as prefect of Changzhou and intendant for ever-normal granaries of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Imperial Treasury, then prefect of Changzhou and circuit ever-normal intendant.

sentences.zh: 秀州海鹽民伐桑柘，毀屋廬，莩殣盈野，或食其子持一臂行乞，而州縣方督促捕欠，顥見之蹙然。

translations.literal: In Xiuzhou, Haiyan people cut mulberry and catalpa, destroyed houses; corpses filled the fields and some ate their children, holding an arm to beg—while prefectures and counties still pressed to collect arrears; Hao's brow knit on seeing it.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiuzhou Haiyan people cut trees and destroyed homes; corpses filled the fields and some ate their children begging with an arm—yet counties pressed for arrears; Hao knit his brow.

sentences.zh: 時有旨倚閣夏稅，遂奏乞並閣秋苗，不俟報行之。

translations.literal: At that time there was an order to defer summer tax; he therefore memorialized asking to defer autumn grain as well and enacted it without awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: An order deferred summer tax; he memorialized to defer autumn grain too and enacted without awaiting reply.

sentences.zh: 言者罪其專，移居筠州，已而寢謫命，止削兩秩，而從其蠲閣之請。

translations.literal: Memorializers faulted his usurpation of authority; he was moved to Yunzhou; later the demotion order was suspended—only two ranks were cut, yet his request to defer collection was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Critics faulted his overreach; he was moved to Yunzhou; later demotion was suspended—two ranks cut but deferral was granted.

sentences.zh: 灝既歸里，幅巾深衣，騎驢匡山間，若素隱者。

translations.literal: Hao returned home, plain scarf and deep robe, riding a donkey among Mount Lu's slopes like a lifelong recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Home again, plain scarf and deep robe, riding a donkey on Mount Lu like a recluse.

sentences.zh: 起知信州，改廣西轉運判官，移廣東提點刑獄，告老不赴。

translations.literal: Recalled to administer Xinzhou, changed to Guangxi transport judge, moved to Guangdong judicial intendant—he reported old age and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Xinzhou, made Guangxi transport judge, Guangdong judicial intendant—he pleaded age and would not go.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 灝性行端飭，以孝友稱。

translations.literal: Hao's conduct was proper and disciplined; he was famed for filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was proper and famed for filial piety and brotherly love.

sentences.zh: 朱熹守南康，灝執弟子禮，質疑問難。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi administered Nan'kang, Hao performed the disciple's rites, questioning and seeking difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi held Nan'kang, Hao performed disciple's rites and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 熹之沒，黨禁方厲，灝單車往赴，徘徊不忍去者久之。

translations.literal: When Xi died the faction ban was severe; Hao went alone in a cart to attend the funeral and lingered long, unable to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died the faction ban was fierce; Hao drove alone to the funeral and lingered, unable to leave.
